newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Chile's Frei hold talks on freer trade.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Chile's Frei hold talks on freer trade.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and Chilean President Eduardo Frei held talks on Wednesday on ways to speed up Chile's inclusion into the North American Free Trade Agreement.

After a state arrival ceremony replete with pomp and ceremony, Clinton and Frei sat down in the Oval Office for discussions that were the centerpiece of the first state visit of the president's second term. They were to hold a joint news conference in the afternoon.

Both leaders, during the welcoming ceremony, spoke of the need to promote freer trade among North and South America with an eye toward the second annual Summit of the Americas in Santigao in March 1998.
"We are working to make trade in the Americas more free and fair, the key to jobs and growth and opportunity for all our people in the next century," said Clinton.
Said Frei: "What we need immediately is for our economies to flourish in full freedom, a freedom that allows us to produce and to trade as if there were no frontiers."
Chile was invited to join the North American trade bloc, which links the United States, Canada and Mexico, at the first Summit of the Americas in Miami in December 1994.

But it has declined to go forward until Clinton gets "fast track" authority from Congress to negotiate trade accords. It fears special interest groups could too easily lobby Congress to derail trade pacts without the authority.
Trade between the United States and Chile passed the $6 billion mark last year, with a $1.5 billion trade balance in favor of the United States.

The United States is one of the most important markets for Chilean salmon, wine and and fresh fruit while U.S. companies are among the chief foreign investors in Chile with billions of dollars invested, mainly in mining.
White House spokesman David Johnson said the United States was "determined to move forward on a free trade agreement with Chile."
"We're working and consulting with Congress and interested parties now on the type of authority that the president needs in order to move those negotiations forward," he said.
Besides free trade, Frei said nurturing a powerful spirit of democracy in Latin America and alleviating poverty were important topics on his agenda.
"We cannot go on proclaiming the end of the Cold War. We must get down to the business of building solid democracies that are deeply rooted in the customs and in the people," he said.
Frei, on a four-day visit to the United States, is to address a joint session of Congress on Thursday.
